findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false; logic is inverted and misleading
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` sets `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false on both branches. It always returns false, so the feature-flag check does nothing. Disabling the feature unconditionally is the intent here, but the code reads as if it honours the flag, and the variable name is the opposite of what it holds. It should simply return false, with a comment explaining that SQL expressions are disabled because of CVE-2024-9264. As written, a future maintainer could easily "fix" the branch and re-enable the vulnerable path.

findings.title: Dead SQL-building code left behind the not-implemented stub
findings.body: `TablesList` still builds `SELECT json_serialize_sql('...')` by string concatenation and passes it to a stub DB that always errors. Every call fails, and each failure logs at error level with the raw user SQL. Leaving the injection-prone command construction in place invites someone to wire up a real DB again without re-checking it. Return a not-implemented error up front instead.

findings.title: SQL commands still constructible via UnmarshalSQLCommand path bypassing reader gate
findings.body: The disable gate was added only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (the legacy `rawNode` path used by the expression service and alerting) still calls `NewSQLCommand` without any check. Execution now fails because the DB is a stub, so this is safe today. However, the only protection on that path is the stub, which is fragile. Add the same explicit disable check in `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand`, and add tests asserting that SQL expressions are rejected on both paths.
